whyEn: This chapter is a disguised classification bank: conductive versus sensorineural deafness, the four speech-disorder families, hemi/para/quadriplegia, osteo- versus rheumatoid arthritis, relapsing versus progressive MS — every pair is a ready-made exam question. Layered on top are dense number targets (trisomy 21 and the 40% cardiac figure, CF's 1-in-3,600, Duchenne's 10 per 100,000, spina bifida's latex allergy with 70–90% hydrocephalus) and technique items the practical loves: the 50 cm face-to-face position, the reverse stethoscope, distal-to-proximal contact in autism, jaw-thrust for the Down syndrome airway, and the DNR decision tree. It also carries the profession's ethical spine — bariatric dignity, the duty owed to homeless and financially anxious patients. Home-care technology (ventilators, dialysis, feeding tubes) is deliberately thin here: that depth lives in Chapter 48.
whyZh: 这一章是一座伪装过的分类题库：传导性对感音神经性耳聋、言语障碍四大家族、偏瘫/截瘫/四肢瘫、骨关节炎对类风湿、复发缓解型对进展型MS——每一对都是现成的考题。上面再叠一层密集的数字靶：21三体和40%先心病、囊性纤维化的1/3,600、杜氏的10/10万、脊柱裂的乳胶过敏加70%～90%脑积水；还有实操考偏爱的技术条目：50 cm正面站位、反用听诊器、自闭症的由远及近触碰、唐氏气道的托颌法、DNR决策树。它同时扛着这份职业的伦理脊梁——肥胖患者的尊严、对无家可归者和为钱发愁者的照护义务。居家医疗设备（呼吸机、透析、喂养管）在本章刻意点到为止：深水区在第48章。

areas: Area 8: Health Promotion and Public Safety

sections.titleEn: Hearing Impairments: Two Types, One Toolkit
sections.titleZh: 听力障碍：两种分型，一套工具箱

points.en: The two-way classification is the anchor question: conductive deafness is usually curable and temporary — eardrum injury, infection, or earwax buildup in the external canal; sensorineural deafness is permanent — a lesion or damage to the inner ear or the eighth cranial nerve, whether congenital, from birth injury, or acquired through disease, medication complications, viral infections, or tumours. Presbycusis is the hearing loss of aging; prolonged loud noise causes its own loss.
points.zh: 两分法是必考锚点：传导性耳聋通常可治、属暂时性——鼓膜损伤、感染或外耳道耵聍堆积；感音神经性耳聋是永久性的——内耳或第八对脑神经的病变或损伤，可为先天、产伤，也可由疾病、药物并发症、病毒感染或肿瘤后天造成。老年性耳聋（presbycusis）是衰老带来的听力下降；长期暴露于巨大噪音也会造成损失。

points.en: Presentation spans slight loss to total deafness, with trouble in pitch, volume, and distinguishing speech. Some patients speak without ever having heard speech; others learned speech, then lost hearing — and now speak too loudly. Recognition clues: hearing aids in place, poor pronunciation, or no response to your presence or questions.
points.zh: 表现从轻度下降到全聋不等，音调、音量和言语分辨都可能出问题。有的患者从未听过言语却学会了说话；有的先会说话后失听——于是嗓门大得反常。识别线索：戴着助听器、发音含混、或对你的出现和提问毫无反应。

points.en: Positioning maths: face the patient so your mouth is visible — no exaggerated lip movements, no looking away — and stand about 50 cm directly in front. Since hearing-impaired patients struggle most with higher frequencies, do not just get louder: lower the pitch of your voice; with 80% of hearing loss tied to high-pitched sounds, switching to a team member with a low-pitched voice is a legitimate tactic.
points.zh: 站位的算术：面对患者、让他看得到你的口型——不夸张口型、不扭头——站在正前方约50 cm处。听障患者最吃亏的是高频音，所以别一味加大音量：把嗓音的音调压低；80%的听力损失与听不清高音相关，换一位嗓音低沉的队员来讲话是完全正当的战术。

points.en: Ask the patient outright: 'How would you like to communicate with me?' Options include American Sign Language with an interpreter, family member, or friend as teammate — and if no interpreter is at hand, call the receiving facility early so one ideally arrives before your assessment begins; written questions on paper; gestures and pictures; or simply sending someone to fetch the patient's hearing aid. Only one person should ask the interview questions, speaking into the less-impaired ear or directly in front.
points.zh: 直接问患者：『您希望怎么和我交流？』选项包括：请手语翻译、家人或朋友当队友打美式手语（ASL）——手边没有翻译就尽早打给接收医院，最好在你开始评估前翻译已到位；纸笔笔谈；手势和图片示意；或干脆派人去把患者的助听器取来。提问只能由一个人负责，冲着较好的那只耳朵说，或站在正前方。

points.en: The reverse stethoscope technique: put your stethoscope's earpieces into the patient's ears and speak softly into the diaphragm — it amplifies your voice on the spot. Softly is the operative word: some hearing-impaired patients are overly sensitive to loud sounds close to the ear, so keep a normal tone.
points.zh: 反用听诊器技术：把你听诊器的耳塞塞进患者耳朵，对着膜面轻声说话——现场就是一台扩音器。『轻声』是关键词：部分听障患者对贴耳的大音量反而过度敏感，保持正常语气即可。

points.en: Four hearing-aid types to recognize: in-the-canal / completely-in-the-canal (tiny case partly or fully inside the canal); in-the-ear (shell filling the outer ear); behind-the-ear (plastic case resting behind the ear); and the conventional body type — the older style, generally for profound hearing loss. A hearing aid makes sound louder; it never restores normal hearing.
points.zh: 四种助听器要认得出：耳道式／完全耳道式（小壳部分或全部藏进耳道）、耳内式（外耳里的一体壳）、耳背式（挂在耳后的塑料壳）、传统体挂式——老式机型，一般用于重度听力丧失。助听器只是把声音放大，永远无法把听力恢复到正常。

points.en: Insertion and failure rules: follow the ear's natural shape, snug but never forced; whistling means the seal is incomplete or the volume too high — reposition, or remove and turn it down. After two failed insertion attempts, stop: box the aid, bring it along, and document its transfer to hospital staff. Never clean a hearing aid and never get it wet.
points.zh: 佩戴与放弃的规则：顺着耳朵的自然形状放入，贴合但绝不硬塞；出现啸叫说明没戴到位没形成密封、或音量开得太大——重新调整位置，或取下调低音量。尝试两次仍装不进就收手：装盒随车带走，并记录移交给医院人员。助听器绝不能清洗，绝不能沾水。

points.en: Dead hearing-aid troubleshooting, in order: confirm it is switched on; try a fresh battery; check the tubing for twists or bends; make sure the switch sits on M (microphone), not T (telephone); for a body aid, swap in a spare cord (the old one may be broken or shorted); and check the ear mould for wax plugging.
points.zh: 助听器不响的排查顺序：确认开机；换新电池；检查导管有无扭折；确认开关拨在 M（麦克风）而不是 T（电话）挡；体挂式换根备用导线（旧线可能断路或短路）；再看耳模是否被耵聍堵住。

sections.titleEn: Speech Impairments and Language Barriers: Four Disorder Families
sections.titleZh: 言语障碍与语言壁垒：四大障碍家族

points.en: Articulation disorders cause the majority of speech difficulties. Dysarthria — the inability to make speech sounds correctly — stems from deficient muscle control and coordination of the larynx, tongue, mouth, and lips: speech comes out slurred, indistinct, slow, or nasal. Typical origins: damaged nerve pathways from brain to those muscles, delayed development from hearing problems, or slow nervous-system maturation from brain damage or motor disability. Both children and adults are affected.
points.zh: 构音障碍占言语困难的大多数。构音困难（dysarthria）——无法正确发出语音——源于喉、舌、口、唇的肌肉控制与协调不足：说出来的话含混、不清、缓慢或带鼻音。常见来源：脑到这些肌肉的神经通路受损、听力问题拖累的发育迟缓、或脑损伤/运动残障导致的神经系统成熟缓慢。儿童和成人都会中招。

points.en: Language disorders mean aphasia: loss of the ability to communicate in speech, writing, or signs, caused by damage to the brain's language centre — stroke, traumatic head or brain injury, brain tumour, delayed development, hearing loss, lack of stimulation, or emotional disturbance. Severity runs from mild to near-total, and it can hit a single facet: recalling object names, building sentences, or reading.
points.zh: 语言障碍指失语症（aphasia）：丧失用言语、书写或手势沟通的能力，源于大脑语言中枢受损——卒中、颅脑外伤、脑肿瘤、发育迟缓、听力丧失、缺乏刺激或情绪障碍。轻重不一，从轻微到几乎无法沟通，也可能只打击单一侧面：想不起物品名称、组不成句子、或读不了字。

points.en: Aphasia interaction inverts a chapter-10 habit: talk to the patient as an adult, use FOCUSED questions rather than open-ended ones, and minimize background noise. The open-ended default gives way when the language machinery itself is broken.
points.zh: 与失语患者的交流把第10章的习惯反了过来：把患者当成年人对待，用『聚焦式』提问而不是开放式提问，并把背景噪音降到最低。当语言机器本身坏了，开放式提问的默认设置就得让位。

points.en: Fluency disorders break, interrupt, or repeat the speech pattern — stuttering is the exemplar: it may surface only on certain words or sounds, worsens under stress, is normal in young children and fades with time, and its specific causes are unknown. Patience is the key: showing impatience or interrupting frustrates the patient and makes the stutter — and your history-taking — worse.
points.zh: 流畅性障碍让语流断裂、中断或重复——口吃是代表：可能只在特定词或音上出现，压力下加重，幼儿口吃属正常并随时间消退，其确切成因不明。关键是耐心：不耐烦或打断只会让患者更受挫，口吃更重，你的病史采集也更难。

points.en: Voice production disorders change how the voice sounds — hoarseness, harshness, inappropriate pitch, abnormal nasal resonance — from vocal-cord closure, hormonal or psychiatric disturbance, or severe hearing loss. Hypernasality can complicate a cleft palate (the palate's two sides failing to fuse midline in utero) or accompany enlarged adenoids.
points.zh: 发声障碍改变的是声音本身——嘶哑、粗粝、音调失当、鼻共鸣异常——原因包括声带闭合问题、内分泌或精神障碍、重度听力丧失。鼻音过重可见于腭裂（胎儿期腭部两侧未在中线融合）或腺样体肥大。

points.en: The laryngitis ladder ends in cancer: acute laryngitis follows voice overuse, throat infection, heavy smoking, smoke inhalation, allergic reaction, or fume exposure. Chronic laryngitis points to long-term irritant exposure and can breed laryngeal polyps — more common in men, with progressive hoarseness the usual chief complaint. The most ominous cause is carcinoma of the larynx: treatment may be partial or total laryngectomy, and total removal leaves aphonia — no normal speech sounds — with a stoma, communication continuing by burping sounds or an electronic or mechanical device.
points.zh: 喉炎的阶梯尽头是癌：急性喉炎见于用嗓过度、咽喉感染、重度吸烟、烟雾吸入、过敏反应或接触刺激性气体。慢性喉炎提示长期刺激物暴露，可长出喉息肉——男性更多见，主诉通常是进行性声嘶。最凶险的病因是喉癌：治疗可能是部分或全喉切除，全切后患者失音（aphonia）——发不出正常语音——颈部留造口，靠打嗝式发声或电子/机械装置继续交流。

points.en: Speech-impairment interaction rules: ask how the patient is most comfortable communicating, allow real time for the answer, listen hard, or enlist someone who knows them (small children's speech often resolves on its own but defeats strangers). Offer pencil and paper, repeat back what you heard for correction — and never speak for the patient or finish their sentences.
points.zh: 与言语障碍患者的交流规则：先问他最舒服的交流方式，留足时间等回答，用心听，或找熟悉患者的人来当翻译（小孩子的言语问题多会自愈，但陌生人往往听不懂）。递上纸笔，把听到的复述回去供他纠正——绝不替患者说话，绝不替他把句子说完。

points.en: The non-English speaker still gets a full history — the step cannot be skipped. Sequence: establish how much English the patient speaks; use short, simple questions and plain words; skip medical terminology; point to body parts as you ask. Document every use of an interpreter or signer, and remember that conclusions based on interpreted information may not be valid.
points.zh: 不会英语的患者照样要采完整病史——这一步不能跳。顺序：先摸清患者会多少英语；用短句、简单词提问；不用医学术语；边问边指身体部位。凡借助翻译或手语者都要记录在案，并且记住：基于转译信息得出的结论未必可靠。

sections.titleEn: Visual Impairments and Paralysis: Guide, Announce, Protect
sections.titleZh: 视力障碍与瘫痪：引导、预告、保护

points.en: Visual impairment arises from congenital defects, disease, injury, infection (cytomegalovirus is the named example), or degeneration of the eyeball, optic nerve, or nerve pathway with aging. Blindness ranges from partial to total: some lose peripheral or central vision, others distinguish only light from dark or general shapes.
points.zh: 视力障碍可来自先天缺陷、疾病、外伤、感染（原书点名巨细胞病毒）、或眼球/视神经/视路随年龄的退变。盲的程度从部分到全盲：有人丢的是周边或中心视野，有人只剩明暗感或大致轮廓。

points.en: Recognition and entry ritual: look for eyeglasses, a white cane, or a service dog; make yourself known when entering, introduce yourself and everyone present (or have them self-introduce) so the patient can map voices to places, and retrieve the patient's visual aids. Crash scenes are doubly disorienting for a patient who compensates with hearing, touch, and smell — so narrate what is happening, identify noises, and describe the surroundings, especially before you move them.
points.zh: 识别与进场仪式：找眼镜、白手杖或导盲犬；进屋先出声报到，介绍自己和在场每个人（或请他们自报），让患者把声音和方位对上号，并把患者的视觉辅助器具找来。事故现场对靠听觉、触觉和嗅觉代偿的患者是双重迷宫——所以要实况解说正在发生什么、指认各种声响、描述周围环境，移动患者前尤其如此。

points.en: Service-dog rules: it is a working dog — no crew member or bystander plays with or distracts it without the patient's permission. Unless the patient is critical, the dog stays in the room, reassures the patient, and prevents transport delays; in some provinces service animals ride in the ambulance with the patient, and if care for the dog must be arranged, a friend or an animal control officer can help.
points.zh: 导盲犬守则：它是正在上班的工作犬——未经患者允许，队员和旁观者都不得逗弄或分散它的注意力。只要患者不是危重，狗就留在原地，既安抚患者又避免转运被拖延；部分省份允许服务犬随患者上救护车；若需要安置狗，可找朋友或动物管理员帮忙。

points.en: Guiding technique: even a stretcher-bound patient's cane, walker, and eyeglasses travel with them. An ambulatory patient is led by a light touch on the arm or elbow, or rests a hand on your shoulder for balance and security — ask which they prefer. Guide gently, never push, and call out obstacles in advance: 'You're approaching the stairs', plus how many to expect.
points.zh: 引导技术：就算患者是躺担架走的，手杖、助行器和眼镜也必须随行。可行走的患者，用手轻搭其手臂或肘部来引路，或让他把手搭在你肩上找平衡和安全感——问他偏好哪种。轻柔引导，绝不推搡，障碍要提前口头预告：『前面到楼梯了』，再加一句有几级。

points.en: Paralysis — inability to voluntarily move one or more body parts — follows head trauma, stroke, spinal cord injury, malignancy, neuromuscular disease, trauma, or birth defects. Sensation is NOT always lost: some patients keep normal feeling, and some have hyperesthesia, where your touch registers as pain. One-sided facial paralysis creates its own communication hurdles.
points.zh: 瘫痪——无法随意移动一个或多个身体部位——见于颅脑外伤、卒中、脊髓损伤、恶性肿瘤、神经肌肉疾病、外伤或出生缺陷。感觉『不一定』丧失：有的患者感觉完好，有的是感觉过敏（hyperesthesia）——你的触碰在他那里就是疼。单侧面瘫还会自带沟通障碍。

points.en: The three-level vocabulary: hemiplegia — one side of the body, typically stroke or head injury; paraplegia — the lower body, typically thoracic or lumbar spinal injury or spina bifida; quadriplegia — all four extremities and the trunk, typically cervical spine injury.
points.zh: 三级词汇表：偏瘫（hemiplegia）——身体一侧，常见于卒中或头部外伤；截瘫（paraplegia）——下半身，常见于胸腰段脊髓损伤或脊柱裂；四肢瘫（quadriplegia）——四肢加躯干，常见于颈髓损伤。

points.en: Equipment and airway hazards travel with paralysis: diaphragmatic involvement may demand a ventilator, and patients may carry halo traction, Foley catheters, tracheotomies, colostomies, or feeding tubes — each device with its own complications (home-care depth belongs to Chapter 48). Dysphagia — inability to swallow from partial esophageal paralysis — makes choking and aspiration easy and emergency airway intervention likely.
points.zh: 瘫痪常拖着一串设备和气道隐患：膈肌受累可能需要呼吸机，患者身上还可能带着 halo 牵引架、Foley 尿管、气管切开、结肠造口或喂养管——每样设备都有自己的并发症（居家设备的深水区在第48章）。吞咽困难（dysphagia）——食管部分瘫痪导致无法吞咽——让呛噎和误吸变得轻而易举，紧急气道干预随时可能上演。

points.en: Handling doctrine: a patient without sensation cannot tell you when you are hurting them, so lift and move with deliberate care; recruit extra team members and plan so no device is dislodged, padding pillows strategically. Paralyzed limbs lack muscle tone — start IVs and give medications on the NONaffected side whenever possible, and check IV sites frequently for infiltration, especially after drug administration.
points.zh: 搬运信条：失去感觉的患者没法告诉你『你正在弄疼我』，抬动都要格外用心；多叫人手、先做规划，别扯脱任何设备，垫枕垫料放到点上。瘫痪的肢体没有肌张力——静脉通路和给药尽量放在『健侧』，并勤查穿刺点有无外渗，给药之后尤其要看。

sections.titleEn: Bariatric Patients: Numbers, Moving Plans, Pickwickian Syndrome
sections.titleZh: 肥胖患者：定义数字、搬运计划与匹克威克综合征

points.en: Definitions carry numbers: obese means 20% to 30% over ideal weight; severe or morbid obesity means 20 to 40 kg over ideal weight. Obesity afflicts roughly one-quarter of all Canadians, and bariatrics is the branch of medicine that studies and treats these patients.
points.zh: 定义自带数字：肥胖指超出理想体重20%～30%；重度／病态肥胖指超出理想体重20～40 kg。肥胖困扰着约四分之一的加拿大人；专门研究和治疗肥胖患者的医学分支叫肥胖医学（bariatrics）。

points.en: The causes table goes beyond diet and exercise: hormonal changes, inadequate sleep, low basal metabolic rate, environmental toxins, genetic predisposition — plus two exam-worthy oddities, cessation or reduction of cigarette smoking and widespread dependence on air conditioning. Causes are often not fully understood.
points.zh: 成因表远不止吃多动少：内分泌变化、睡眠不足、基础代谢率低、环境毒素、遗传易感——外加两个容易出题的冷门项：戒烟/减烟，以及对空调的普遍依赖。肥胖的成因常常并未完全弄清。

points.en: Interaction context: many patients carry embarrassment and fear of ridicule — some inflicted by insensitive health care professionals. Put them at ease early, establish the chief complaint, communicate your plan, and expect a complex, extensive medical history that rewards good interviewing.
points.zh: 交流的背景板：不少患者背着难堪和被嘲笑的恐惧——有些正是拜不体贴的医疗人员所赐。尽早让他放松，先确立主诉，讲明你的处置计划，并预期一份复杂冗长的既往史——问诊功夫好的人在这里占便宜。

points.en: Moving rules: call early for extra help; use the purpose-built kit — inflatable mats, larger polypropylene sheets, higher-load stretchers with adjustable side supports, pneumatic stretchers, bariatric ambulances; never lift by a single limb (overtaxed joints injure easily — many patients already have chronic joint injuries or osteoarthritis from pulling, rocking, and rolling into position); brief every move to the whole team first; if a move goes uncontrolled — stop, reposition, resume.
points.zh: 搬运规则：尽早呼叫增援；用专门装备——充气垫、大号聚丙烯滑布、高承重可调侧挡担架、气动担架、肥胖专用救护车；绝不抓单个肢体去抬（长期靠拉拽、摇晃、翻滚挪动身体的患者，关节早已慢性劳损甚至骨关节炎，一抬就伤）；每一步搬运先向全组交底；过程一旦失控——停下、重新摆位、再继续。

points.en: Safety details that get tested: watch for pinch and pressure points from equipment — they can cause deep venous thrombosis; very large patients may struggle to breathe lying flat, so position accordingly; know your equipment's weight limits; plan egress routes for patient, gear, and lifting crew; and notify the receiving facility early so special arrangements are ready on arrival.
points.zh: 爱出题的安全细节：提防设备造成的夹压点——可诱发深静脉血栓；超大体型患者平躺可能喘不上气，摆位要留心；清楚自家器材的承重上限；出口路线要按患者、装备加搬运人手一起规划；并提前通知接收医院，让特殊安排在你到达前就绪。

points.en: Obesity hypoventilation (Pickwickian) syndrome hits the extremely obese with a triad — hypoxemia (deficient blood oxygenation), hypercapnia (excess CO2), and polycythemia (overproduction of red cells). Findings: headache, apnea especially during sleep, sleepiness, red face, muscle twitching, and signs of right-side heart failure — some demanding prehospital emergency intervention. The ultimate remedy is weight reduction, via monitored diet or gastric bypass surgery, though surgery carries a high complication risk and suits only some candidates.
points.zh: 肥胖低通气（匹克威克）综合征打击极度肥胖者，三联征——低氧血症（血液氧合不足）、高碳酸血症（CO2过多）、红细胞增多症（红细胞过量生成）。表现：头痛、呼吸暂停（睡眠中尤甚）、嗜睡、面色发红、肌肉抽动，以及右心衰体征——其中一些需要院前紧急干预。根治之道是减重：严密监控的饮食，或胃旁路手术——但手术并发症风险高，且并非人人适合。

sections.titleEn: Mental Challenges: Developmental Disability, Down Syndrome, Autism
sections.titleZh: 心智挑战：发育障碍、唐氏综合征与自闭谱系

points.en: Mental illness is a generic term for illnesses producing emotional, cognitive, or behavioural dysfunction — it can occur in people with or without an existing disability, and mental status and physical well-being influence each other in both directions. The body's stress response can distort the assessment, altering respiratory rate, heart rate, or the patient's perception of physical illness — so a detailed history is the anchor, and treatment and transport centre on the chief complaint with supportive care.
points.zh: 精神疾病是个统称，涵盖造成情绪、认知或行为功能障碍的各种疾病——有无原发残障的人都可能患上，而且心理状态与身体健康互相影响、双向拉扯。应激反应会搅乱你的评估——呼吸、心率乃至患者对身体不适的感知都可能被改写——所以详细病史才是锚，治疗和转运围绕主诉展开，配合支持性照护。

points.en: Baseline first: with an emotionally or intellectually disabled patient, establish their normal emotional and mental ability from patient or caregiver so you can spot changes. Speak calmly even if the patient may not understand, and explain each action before doing it. Watch for clenched fists and aggressive or agitated movements or speech — they may be your only warning of an impending confrontation.
points.zh: 先立基线：面对情绪或智力障碍的患者，先从本人或照护者那里弄清他平时的情绪与心智水平，之后才谈得上识别『变化』。哪怕患者可能听不懂，也要用平静的语气说话，每个动作先解释再动手。同时盯住攥拳、激越的动作或言语——那可能是冲突逼近前你能得到的唯一警告。

points.en: Canadian terminology puts the person first: 'persons with disabilities'. A developmental disability is a permanent condition in which a person develops more slowly and differently, with difficulty learning, processing abstract ideas, and adapting to daily life. Causes span genetics, congenital infections, birth complications, malnutrition, environmental factors, prenatal drug or alcohol use (fetal alcohol syndrome), and postnatal traumatic brain injury or poisoning such as lead.
points.zh: 加拿大的规范用语把『人』放在前面：persons with disabilities（有障碍的人）。发育障碍是一种终身状况：发育更慢、路径不同，学习、抽象思维和适应日常生活都吃力。成因横跨遗传因素、先天感染、分娩并发症、营养不良、环境因素、产前药物或酒精暴露（胎儿酒精综合征），以及出生后的颅脑外伤或铅等中毒。

points.en: Assessment without an IQ test: simply talking to the patient and family reveals how well they understand and interact. Slight impairment shows as slowness to understand, limited vocabulary, and immaturity next to peers; a severely disabled person may be unable to care for themselves, communicate, understand, or respond to surroundings. A roomful of emergency strangers breaks routine and can overwhelm — anxiety climbs, interaction worsens.
points.zh: 不用智商测验的评估：跟患者和家属聊几句，就能大致摸清他的理解和互动水平。轻度障碍表现为反应偏慢、词汇量有限、比同龄人显得幼稚；重度障碍者可能无法自理、无法交流、无法理解或回应周围环境。急救队伍一屋子陌生人本身就是对日常规律的打破，足以把患者淹没——焦虑越升，互动越难。

points.en: Down syndrome arithmetic: the normal somatic cell has 23 chromosomes; in trisomy 21, chromosome 21 fails to separate, the ovum carries 24, and fertilization by a normal 23-chromosome sperm produces a triplicated chromosome 21. Known risk factors: maternal age over 35 and a family history of Down syndrome.
points.zh: 唐氏综合征的算术：正常体细胞含23条染色体；21三体的机制是第21号染色体未分离，卵子带了24条，再与正常23条染色体的精子受精，第21号染色体便成了三份。已知危险因素：母亲年龄超过35岁，以及唐氏综合征家族史。

points.en: The Down syndrome feature list reads straight onto exams: round head with flat occiput; enlarged protruding tongue; slanted wide-set eyes with skin folds covering the inner corners; short broad hands; small face and features; congenital heart defects; thyroid problems; hearing and vision problems. No patient has all of them — the combination is distinctive enough that diagnosis is usually rapid at birth.
points.zh: 唐氏面容清单直接对接考题：圆头伴扁平后枕、增大且外伸的舌头、眼裂上斜且眼距宽、内眦被皮肤皱襞覆盖、手短而宽、脸小五官小、先天性心脏缺陷、甲状腺问题、听力与视力问题。没有哪个患者集齐全部——但组合的辨识度高到通常出生时即可迅速确诊。

points.en: Up to 40% of patients with Down syndrome have congenital heart disease — endocardial cushion defects, ventricular or atrial septal defects — so emergency care includes airway management, supplemental oxygen, and IV access; in heart failure, give diuretics with judicious fluid resuscitation only if necessary.
points.zh: 多达40%的唐氏患者患先天性心脏病——心内膜垫缺损、室间隔或房间隔缺损——因此急救处置包含气道管理、补充给氧和静脉通路；出现心衰时用利尿剂，液体复苏须谨慎、确有必要才做。

points.en: The Down syndrome airway is a known trap: large tongue plus small oral and nasal cavities make bag-mask ventilation and intubation difficult, and malocclusions add dental anomalies (and speech abnormalities). For airway obstruction a simple jaw-thrust may be all that is needed; in the unconscious patient, jaw-thrust or a nasopharyngeal airway. Epilepsy is common in Down syndrome — mostly tonic–clonic seizures, managed the same as in any other patient.
points.zh: 唐氏气道是有名的陷阱：大舌头配小口腔小鼻腔，球囊面罩通气和插管都难，咬合不正又添牙列异常（连带言语异常）。气道梗阻时，一个简单的托颌法可能就够；患者昏迷时，用托颌法或鼻咽通气道。癫痫在唐氏人群中常见——多为强直阵挛型，处理与其他癫痫患者相同。

points.en: Autism spectrum disorders are complex disorders of brain development marked by difficulty with social interaction, repetitive behaviours, and verbal and nonverbal communication, now diagnosed more often — from better screening, a true rise, or both. Many patients are nonverbal lifelong or become nonverbal under stress; developmental regression in a young child without another cause should raise the possibility of autism. Cognition spans intellectual disability to highly sophisticated skill with mathematics, puzzles, memory, or art.
points.zh: 自闭谱系障碍是脑发育的复杂病变，标志是社交互动困难、重复刻板行为、言语与非言语沟通障碍，确诊率在上升——可能因筛查变好、发病真增多，或两者皆有。许多患者终生不语，或在应激时段失语；幼儿出现无其他原因可解释的发育倒退，就要想到自闭症。认知跨度极大：从达到智力障碍标准，到在数学、拼图、记忆或艺术上技惊四座。

points.en: Autism contact protocol: commotion and excess stimuli can trigger bizarre or aggressive behaviour, so quiet the scene. Explain before every touch and move contact from DISTAL to PROXIMAL; repeat questions in several different phrasings and check for a consistent response. Pain perception is unreliable in both directions — minimal reaction to a serious injury, or great discomfort from minor contact. Bring the caregivers into assessment, treatment, and transport.
points.zh: 自闭症接触规程：喧闹和过量刺激可诱发怪异或攻击行为，先把现场静下来。每次触碰前先解释，接触顺序从『远端到近端』；同一个问题换几种问法重复，核对回答是否一致。痛觉两头都靠不住——重伤可以几乎没反应，轻碰反而痛苦不堪。把照护者拉进评估、治疗和转运的全程。

points.en: The staged-approach script for developmental disability: hold the team back while one paramedic builds rapport, then introduce members one at a time and explain each task — let the patient see and touch the blood pressure cuff before it goes on, shake hands if permitted, move slowly but deliberately. Trust built early is what lets you later do the painful things, like starting an IV. Feeling awkward is normal; treating the patient as you would anyone else is the best plan.
points.zh: 发育障碍的分步接近脚本：全队先按住阵脚，由一名救护员建立融洽关系，再把队员一个个介绍进场、逐项解释要做什么——量血压前先让患者看一看、摸一摸袖带，对方允许就握个手，动作放慢但果断。前期攒下的信任，是你之后做疼痛操作（比如打静脉）的本钱。感到不自在很正常；把患者当普通人对待就是最好的方案。

sections.titleEn: Pathologic Challenges I: Arthritis, Cancer, Cerebral Palsy, Cystic Fibrosis
sections.titleZh: 病理性挑战（上）：关节炎、癌症、脑瘫、囊性纤维化

points.en: The chapter's pathology roster: arthritis, cancer, cerebral palsy, cystic fibrosis, multiple sclerosis, muscular dystrophy, poliomyelitis, previous head injury, spina bifida, and myasthenia gravis — and many of these patients know the progression and nuances of their own condition better than you do. Use that expertise.
points.zh: 本章的病理清单：关节炎、癌症、脑瘫、囊性纤维化、多发性硬化、肌营养不良、脊髓灰质炎、既往颅脑损伤、脊柱裂、重症肌无力——而且这些患者中许多人对自身疾病的进展和细节比你更门儿清。用好这份专长。

points.en: Arthritis tells apart on mechanism: osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease of aging that first targets the lower-extremity joints, with pain growing through the day and stiffness worst after prolonged rest; rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disorder that inflames and destroys joints and connective tissue, running from remission periods to rapid progression. Both erode range of motion and set patients up for falls. Field rules: ask about current medications before adding any, move with minimal discomfort, and use equipment that actually fits.
points.zh: 关节炎按机制区分：骨关节炎是随衰老而来的退行性关节病，最先侵犯下肢关节，疼痛随一天推移加重、久歇后僵硬最明显；类风湿关节炎是自身免疫病，让关节和结缔组织发炎、被破坏，病程从缓解期到快速进展不等。两者都蚕食活动度、抬高跌倒风险。现场规则：给任何药之前先问清正在用什么药，搬动时把不适降到最低，器材要用尺寸合身的。

points.en: Cancer in two lines: uncontrolled overgrowth of normal tissue cells that, unchecked, spreads, destroys body systems, and kills; more than 200 kinds are believed to exist, each named for where it originates. Treatment may run a single pathway or a complex orchestration — surgery (long a primary method), medications, radiation, chemotherapy.
points.zh: 两句话说完癌症：正常组织细胞的失控过度增生，不加遏制就会扩散、摧毁身体系统、致人死亡；已知的癌症种类被认为超过200种，均按起源部位命名。治疗可以是单一路径，也可以是复杂的组合拳——手术（长期以来的主要手段之一）、药物、放疗、化疗。

points.en: Cerebral palsy definition dissects into exam phrases: a NONprogressive, BILATERAL neuromuscular disorder of poorly controlled voluntary muscles, from developmental brain insults in utero (cerebral hypoxia, maternal infection, kernicterus), brain trauma at birth or in early childhood, or postpartum infections (encephalitis, meningitis). Hallmarks: spastic limb movements and poor posture; related complications include visual impairment, hearing and language difficulties, seizures, and developmental disability.
points.zh: 脑瘫的定义可拆成考点短语：『非进行性』『双侧性』的神经肌肉障碍，随意肌控制不良，源于宫内脑损害（脑缺氧、母体感染、核黄疸）、出生时或幼年期脑外伤、或产后感染（脑炎、脑膜炎）。标志：肢体痉挛性动作与不良姿势；相关并发症包括视力障碍、听力语言困难、癫痫和发育障碍。

points.en: Cerebral palsy numbers that flip assumptions: 75% of patients have some intellectual disability — which means a quarter do not, so never assume; about 25% also have seizures, so keep suction within reach. Limbs are underdeveloped and injury-prone (wheelchair falls), walking patients have an ataxic, unsteady gait, and many live near-normal independent lives on computerized aids and joystick- or mouth-controlled wheelchairs.
points.zh: 颠覆预设的脑瘫数字：75%的患者有某种程度的智力障碍——反过来说有四分之一没有，所以绝不能想当然；约25%合并癫痫，吸引器要放在手边。肢体发育不良、易受伤（从轮椅上跌落是典型），能行走者步态共济失调、不稳易摔；许多患者靠计算机化辅具和摇杆/口控电动轮椅过着接近正常的独立生活。

points.en: Cerebral palsy transport rules: let the patient keep their custom-shaped chair or pillow during transport, pad for comfort, NEVER force extremities into position, and take walkers and wheelchairs along whenever possible.
points.zh: 脑瘫转运规则：转运时让患者继续用他定制的座椅或枕头，垫护到位，『绝不』把肢体硬掰进某个姿势，助行器和轮椅能带则带。

points.en: Cystic fibrosis (mucoviscidosis) is a chronic endocrine-system dysfunction hitting mainly the respiratory and digestive systems: about 1 in every 3,600 children born in Canada has CF, most commonly Caucasians of Northern European descent. It is usually fatal — most affected children do not live past their teens, though aggressive management can extend life well into the 30s.
points.zh: 囊性纤维化（黏稠物阻塞症）是内分泌系统的慢性功能障碍，主攻呼吸和消化系统：加拿大每3,600名新生儿约有1人患病，北欧裔白人最常见。通常致命——多数患儿活不过十几岁，但激进的管理与监测可把生命延长到30多岁。

points.en: CF mechanism to findings: a defective recessive gene impedes chloride movement through cells — sodium loss runs unusually high (salty skin) and mucus secretions turn abnormally thick. In the lungs that mucus obstructs breathing and grows bacteria, so infection susceptibility soars and lung disease becomes the primary cause of death; in the gut it brings malnutrition, poor growth, and intestinal blockages. Findings: tachypnea, productive cough, shortness of breath, barrel chest, clubbed fingers, cyanosis. Field care: treat the chief complaint; watch for respiratory insufficiency, infection signs, intestinal blockage, and dysrhythmias from electrolyte imbalance; suction, high-flow oxygen, and breathing therapies may be needed in transport.
points.zh: 囊性纤维化从机制到体征：缺陷的隐性基因阻碍氯离子跨细胞转运——钠丢失异常增多（皮肤发咸），黏液分泌异常黏稠。在肺里，这层黏液既堵气道又养细菌，感染易感性飙升，肺部病变成为首要死因；在肠道则带来营养不良、生长迟缓和肠梗阻。体征：呼吸急促、咳痰、气短、桶状胸、杵状指、发绀。现场处置：围绕主诉治疗；警惕呼吸功能不全、感染征象、肠梗阻和电解质紊乱引发的心律失常；转运途中可能用到吸引、高流量给氧和呼吸治疗。

sections.titleEn: Pathologic Challenges II: MS, Muscular Dystrophy, Polio, Spina Bifida, Head Injury, Myasthenia Gravis
sections.titleZh: 病理性挑战（下）：多发性硬化、肌营养不良、脊髓灰质炎、脊柱裂、颅脑伤后、重症肌无力

points.en: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic central nervous system disease destroying myelin and nerve axons in brain and spinal cord — an autoimmune disorder with no known cause, sometimes genetically inherited. It strikes women in their 20s to 40s two to three times more often than men; Canadians have one of the world's highest MS rates, three new cases are diagnosed every day, and it is the most common neurologic disease of Canadian adults.
points.zh: 多发性硬化是中枢神经系统的慢性病，破坏脑和脊髓内的髓鞘与轴突——自身免疫性疾病，病因不明，部分有遗传性。20～40多岁的女性发病率是男性的2～3倍；加拿大的MS发病率位居世界前列，每天新确诊3例，它是加拿大成人最常见的神经系统疾病。

points.en: MS mechanism explains the name: patches of myelin inflame at random sites, detach from the axon, self-destruct, and scar over — multiple (many) plus sclerosis (to harden). Two forms: relapsing/remitting in 90% of patients (bouts of worsening, then marked improvement with lingering stiffness and weakness in some) and progressive in 10% (relentless worsening, no relief). Untreated, one-half of relapsing/remitting patients convert to the progressive form within 15 years.
points.zh: MS的机制就藏在病名里：髓鞘在随机部位发炎、从轴突上剥离、自毁、瘢痕化——multiple（多处）加 sclerosis（硬化）。两种类型：复发缓解型占90%（症状阵发加重后明显好转，部分人遗留僵硬无力）；进展型占10%（持续恶化、没有喘息）。不治疗的话，复发缓解型患者中有一半会在15年内转为进展型。

points.en: MS signs sort by location — brain: slurred speech, confusion, forgetfulness, pain, depression; spinal cord: stiffness, muscle spasms, bowel and bladder problems, sexual dysfunction, paralysis, numbness, muscle weakness; plus tingling, unexplained weakness, dizziness, fatigue, double or blurry vision. No cure exists — treatments cut attack frequency; your care is supportive, often for tertiary complications like falls, and absent sensation can hide findings, so the detailed history carries the exam.
points.zh: MS体征按部位分拣——脑部：言语含糊、意识混乱、健忘、疼痛、抑郁；脊髓：僵硬、肌肉痉挛、大小便问题、性功能障碍、瘫痪、麻木、肌无力；另有针刺感、不明原因无力、眩晕、疲乏、复视或视物模糊。无法治愈——治疗只能减少发作；你的处置以支持为主，常是为跌倒这类三级并发症出勤，而感觉缺失会藏起体征，详细病史才是主角。

points.en: Muscular dystrophy: an inherited disease of progressive muscle-fibre degeneration, destroyed fibres often replaced by fat or connective tissue — muscles weaken, motor development slows, contractility fades. More than 30 types exist: some start in early childhood and progress fast, others surface from the late teens into the 40s and creep. Duchenne, the most common, affects 10 of every 100,000 male births.
points.zh: 肌营养不良：遗传性疾病，肌纤维进行性变性，坏死的纤维常被脂肪或结缔组织顶替——肌肉渐弱、运动发育放缓、收缩力消退。类型超过30种：有的幼年起病、进展迅猛，有的十八九岁到四十多岁才冒头、进展缓慢。最常见的杜氏型（Duchenne），每10万名男婴中有10人患病。

points.en: Muscular dystrophy's grim numbers: first clues are delayed landmarks — sitting, walking, climbing stairs; kyphoscoliosis (upper-spine hump with lower-spine curvature) squeezes pulmonary function; cardiac involvement appears in as many as 95% of patients; and only 25% of those affected live to age 21, with pulmonary or cardiac complications the usual cause of death.
points.zh: 肌营养不良的残酷数字：最早的线索是里程碑延迟——坐、走、爬楼梯都晚；脊柱后侧凸（上段驼峰加下段弯曲）压缩肺功能；心脏受累的比例可高达95%；患者中只有25%能活到21岁，死因通常是肺部或心脏并发症。

points.en: Polio's Canadian timeline is pure exam bait: first identified in 1789; last major Canadian epidemic 1959 with 1,887 paralytic cases; Salk and Sabin vaccines released 1955; Canada declared polio-free in 1994; live vaccine unused in Canada since 1996. Today's Canadian cases are polio-infected visitors or vaccine-associated paralytic polio from contact with someone recently given live vaccine — still administered elsewhere in the world, where lapsed programs, civil unrest, and migration keep sporadic outbreaks alive.
points.zh: 脊髓灰质炎的加拿大时间线全是考题素材：1789年首次确认；加拿大最后一次大流行在1959年，报告1,887例麻痹病例；Salk和Sabin疫苗1955年问世；加拿大1994年宣布无脊灰；1996年起加拿大不再使用活疫苗。如今加拿大的病例只有两类：境外输入的感染者，或与新近接种活疫苗者接触引发的疫苗相关麻痹型脊灰——活疫苗在世界不少地方仍在用，免疫规划中断、内乱和人口迁移让零星暴发不断。

points.en: Polio pathophysiology and course: humans are the only known host; the virus enters through the mouth, replicates in pharynx, gastrointestinal tract, and local lymphatics, then rides the bloodstream to the central nervous system. In 80% to 90% of cases — usually young children — illness is mild (malaise, sore throat, headache, vomiting, slight fever), followed by apparent wellness, then days later the major illness: fever, severe headache, stiff neck and back, deep muscle pain, or paralysis. Nonparalytic forms recover completely; weakness or paralysis persisting beyond 12 months after infection marks permanent damage. Sequelae may need tracheal ventilation and indwelling catheters.
points.zh: 脊灰的病理与病程：人类是唯一已知宿主；病毒经口进入，在咽部、胃肠道和局部淋巴系统复制，再随血流直捣中枢神经系统。80%～90%的病例——多为幼儿——只是轻症（不适、咽痛、头痛、呕吐、低热），随后一段『假愈期』，几天后主病杀到：发热、剧烈头痛、颈背强直、深部肌痛乃至瘫痪。非麻痹型可完全康复；感染后无力或瘫痪超过12个月即为永久性损害。后遗症患者可能需要经气管通气和留置导尿。

points.en: Spina bifida is the most common permanently disabling birth defect — about 120 children born with it in Canada each year. In the first month of pregnancy the spinal column fails to close completely, vertebrae do not develop, and part of the cord lies exposed. Folic acid taken faithfully BEFORE pregnancy cuts the risk; other maternal risk factors: a previous neural-tube-defect pregnancy (raises risk by 20%), diabetes, diagnosed obesity, some antiseizure medications, raised temperature in early pregnancy (hot baths, hot tubs, fever), Caucasian or Hispanic ethnicity, and lower socioeconomic status.
points.zh: 脊柱裂是最常见的永久致残性出生缺陷——加拿大每年约有120名新生儿罹患。孕期第一个月脊柱未能完全闭合、椎骨不发育，一段脊髓暴露在外。『怀孕前』坚持服用叶酸能降低风险；其他母体危险因素：既往神经管缺陷妊娠史（风险增加20%）、糖尿病、确诊的肥胖、某些抗癫痫药、孕早期体温升高（热水浴、热水浴缸、发热感染）、白人或西语裔背景、较低的社会经济地位。

points.en: Spina bifida clinical package: partial or full paralysis (usually lower extremities), bladder and bowel control difficulties, learning disabilities — and latex allergy, the detail exams adore. In the most severe form, 70% to 90% of patients have hydrocephalus: excess cerebrospinal fluid pressurizing the brain, relieved by a shunt that stays for life. Care like paralysis care: ask how best to move them, hunt for injuries they cannot feel (including an infiltrated IV), and expect urinary catheters and other aids.
points.zh: 脊柱裂的临床套餐：部分或完全瘫痪（通常在下肢）、大小便控制困难、学习障碍——还有考试最爱的细节：乳胶过敏。最重型患者中70%～90%合并脑积水：过量脑脊液压迫大脑，靠分流管减压，且终身佩戴。照护比照瘫痪患者：先问怎么搬最好，仔细搜寻他感觉不到的损伤（包括外渗的静脉通路），并预期身上有导尿管等辅助装置。

points.en: The previous-head-injury patient: traumatic brain injury leaves long-term cognitive, sensory, communication, motor, behavioural, or psychological deficits. Build the treatment plan on a complete history from patient, family, and friends, and establish what is normal for this patient. Talk calmly and soothingly, watch closely for anxiety or aggression, be ready to position or restrain for mutual safety — and do not expect the patient to walk to the ambulance. Use the name, explain procedures, reassure throughout.
points.zh: 既往颅脑损伤的患者：创伤性脑损伤会留下认知、感觉、沟通、运动、行为或心理层面的长期缺陷。治疗计划要建立在向本人、家属和朋友采集的完整病史之上，先确立『这位患者的正常』是什么样。语气平静安抚，紧盯焦虑或攻击的苗头，必要时为了双方安全摆位或约束——并且别指望患者自己走到救护车。叫他的名字，解释每项操作，全程安抚。

points.en: Myasthenia gravis mechanism in one chain: a rare autoimmune disorder in which antibodies block or damage acetylcholine receptor sites at the nerve junction — impulses fail to reach muscle, producing chronic fatigability and weakness, worst in the face and throat, in sudden bouts during activity that improve with rest. Demographics: most common in women under 40 (typically 20 to 30) and men over 60.
points.zh: 重症肌无力的机制一条链讲完：罕见的自身免疫病——抗体阻断或破坏神经接头处的乙酰胆碱受体位点——冲动传不到肌肉，造成慢性易疲劳和无力，面部和咽喉最重，活动时突发、休息后缓解。人群分布：40岁以下女性（典型20～30岁）和60岁以上男性最常见。

points.en: Myasthenia gravis from first sign to crisis: earliest symptoms are weakness of eye or eyelid movement and altered facial expression; sudden difficulty swallowing or chewing and slurred speech often bring the diagnosis; blurry vision, neck weakness, shortness of breath, and limb weakness follow — a picture easily misattributed, making diagnosis hard. The crisis: respiratory muscles weakened by infection, stress, medication side effects, or even menstruation can collapse into acute respiratory failure — intervene immediately with airway management, ventilatory support, and possibly intubation.
points.zh: 重症肌无力从首发到危象：最早的症状是眼球或眼睑运动无力、面部表情改变；突然的吞咽或咀嚼困难、言语含糊常常才引出诊断；随后是视物模糊、颈部无力、气短、四肢无力——这幅图景极易被归因于别的病，诊断因此困难。危象：感染、应激、药物副作用甚至月经都能把呼吸肌拖垮，急转直下成急性呼吸衰竭——立即介入：气道管理、通气支持，必要时插管。

sections.titleEn: End-of-Life Care: Comfort, DNR Logic, and the Family
sections.titleZh: 临终照护：舒适、DNR 的处置逻辑与家属

points.en: Signs of impending death to recognize on scene: decreased intake of food and drink, decreased orientation, irregular breathing patterns, and bradycardia or tachycardia. Recognizing them changes your role — reassure the family that their loved one will be helped respectfully and with dignity.
points.zh: 现场要认得的濒死征象：进食进水减少、定向力下降、呼吸节律不规则、心动过缓或过速。认出这些征象，你的角色就变了——要向家属保证，会以最尊重、最有尊严的方式帮助他们的亲人。

points.en: What seriously ill patients call a good death, per the text: pain and symptom management, preparation for death, and achieving a sense of completion. Goals split — some terminal patients choose the most aggressive care possible, others choose comfort over cure or prolongation; surprisingly little data describes what families believe makes a good death.
points.zh: 原书里重症患者眼中的『善终』三要素：疼痛与症状控制、为死亡做好准备、获得圆满感。目标因人而异——有的终末期患者选择最激进的治疗，有的要舒适而不求治愈或延命；而关于家属心中何为善终，数据出奇地少。

points.en: Terminally ill patients usually need only supportive care aimed at comfort: a displaced urinary catheter, help returning to bed, or intervention in a pain crisis — often because the hospice or home-health nurse is delayed. Their pain regimens can be complex (medication arrays, transdermal patches, self-administered devices), so consult medical direction for guidance.
points.zh: 终末期患者通常只需要以舒适为目标的支持性照护：复位移位的导尿管、扶回床上、或处理一次疼痛危象——呼叫的原因常常只是安宁疗护或居家护士来晚了。他们的镇痛方案可能很复杂（多种药物、透皮贴剂、自控镇痛装置），要连线医疗指导寻求指引。

points.en: DNR doctrine, textbook version: with a valid do-not-resuscitate order, CPR is not indicated when the heart or breathing stops. ANY question about the order's validity or the patient's intended level of intervention → start resuscitation while contacting direct medical control. When no resuscitation is attempted, aggressive comfort measures are mandatory: oxygen, salbutamol-based breathing treatments, and narcotics for pain and respiratory distress per local protocol, plus comfortable positioning.
points.zh: DNR 的教科书信条：有有效的『不施行心肺复苏』指令时，心跳或呼吸停止不做CPR。但凡对指令效力或患者想要的干预级别存有『任何』疑问→一边开始复苏一边联系直接医疗指挥。不做复苏时，积极的舒适措施是义务：按当地协议给氧、沙丁胺醇类雾化、用麻醉性镇痛药处理疼痛和呼吸窘迫，并摆好舒适体位。

points.en: The DNR-versus-family controversy has a scripted resolution: if the family wants CPR despite a DNR, first make certain they know the order exists; if they still insist once aware, you start resuscitation — because in the field you cannot verify who initiated the order or whether a person with legal medical authority is present, and sorting that out belongs to the emergency physicians. Review the DNR, keep it with the patient during transport, and know in advance your local law and protocol.
points.zh: 家属与DNR冲突时有现成的处置脚本：家属要求CPR而DNR在场，先确保他们知道这份指令的存在；知情后仍坚持，就开始复苏——因为在现场你无法核实指令是谁启动的、有法定医疗决定权的人在不在场，这团乱麻留给急诊医生去解。核看DNR原件、转运全程随患者携带，并且提前吃透本地法规与协议。

points.en: Logistics of a home death: honour the family's choice between keeping the patient at home and transport, provided local or regional protocol allows; let a family member ride along if asked; advise medical control and the receiving hospital en route. Protocols vary — know whether the coroner must be called and by whom, and whether a pronouncement of death is required and who makes it.
points.zh: 居家死亡的后勤题：家属选择让患者留在家中还是送医，只要本地或区域协议允许就应尊重；家属要求随车就让随车；途中通报医疗指挥和接收医院。各地协议不同——要弄清是否必须报告验尸官、由谁联系，以及是否需要宣布死亡、由谁宣布。

points.en: Scene management around a dying patient: chaos and hostility from an overwhelmed family are expected, not exceptional — meet everyone with compassion and understanding, and use team members to separate individuals and talk them down one on one, defusing emotion and restoring order.
points.zh: 濒死现场的秩序管理：被击垮的家属又乱又冲不是意外，是常态——对每个人都拿出同情与体谅，让队友把情绪激动者分开、一对一安抚，先化解情绪，再恢复秩序。

sections.titleEn: Communicable Disease and Financial Worry: Two Duties of Care
sections.titleZh: 传染性疾病与经济顾虑：两份不打折的照护义务

points.en: Routine precautions exist precisely because some patients carry communicable diseases: appropriate personal protective equipment with EVERY patient, EVERY time — gloves and eye protection as basic attire, gowns and masks added when the situation warrants. Safety for you, the crew, and the patient is paramount, and the compassion owed these patients is exactly the same as for anyone else.
points.zh: 常规防护之所以是『常规』，正因为有些患者带着传染性疾病：『每名』患者、『每一次』都要穿戴合适的个人防护装备——手套和护目是基础着装，情况需要时再加隔离衣和口罩。你、队友和患者的安全高于一切；而对这类患者的同情心，一分都不能比别人少。

points.en: Clues that a patient may be infectious: rashes, coughing, an ill appearance, the health or travel history, and the medication list. The reverse manoeuvre matters too: offer an immunocompromised patient a mask BEFORE hospital arrival — masking early in your assessment can be the quickest, easiest block on disease transmission in either direction.
points.zh: 提示患者可能有传染病的线索：皮疹、咳嗽、病容、健康史或旅行史、以及在用药物清单。反向操作同样重要：给免疫功能低下的患者在『到医院之前』就递上口罩——评估早期就戴上口罩，可能是双向阻断疾病传播最快、最省事的一招。

points.en: The financial-anxiety patient — often elderly — may refuse transport with 'I can't go, I don't have the money': they lived before universal health care arrived in Canada, and many hold no private insurance covering ambulance services. The job is careful, compassionate communication: find the source of the anxiety and share your concern about their current health, rather than letting a fear of fees decide a medical outcome.
points.zh: 为钱焦虑的患者——常常是老人——可能用一句『我去不起医院，我没钱』拒绝转运：他们经历过加拿大全民医保建立之前的年代，而且许多人没有覆盖救护车费用的私人保险。你的任务是细致而有同情心的沟通：找到焦虑的源头，把你对他当前健康状况的担忧讲给他听——别让对账单的恐惧替他做医疗决定。

atScene.en: A patient who keeps asking you to repeat yourself is flagging a hearing impairment — borderline cases often do not know their own deficit, and the noisy prehospital scene makes it worse.
atScene.zh: 患者反复请你『再说一遍』，就是在给你打听力障碍的信号——临界程度的患者常常不知道自己听力有多差，而嘈杂的院前环境会雪上加霜。

atScene.en: Sirens are loud enough to cost YOU your hearing — protect it before it is too late, or presbycusis will not wait for retirement.
atScene.zh: 警笛的音量足以搭上『你自己』的听力——趁还来得及做好防护，别等职业性听损提前替你退休。

atScene.en: Approaching a patient with a developmental disability, remember what they see: a stranger in an unexplained uniform arriving with a crowd. Stagger the team's approach — rapport first, introductions one by one — instead of mobbing the patient.
atScene.zh: 接近发育障碍患者时，想想他眼中的画面：一个穿着看不懂的制服的陌生人，还带着一群人围过来。让团队错峰进场——先建立关系，再逐个介绍——而不是一拥而上。

atScene.en: A patient with spina bifida on your stretcher means a latex check on your gloves and equipment — latex allergy is part of the condition's standard package.
atScene.zh: 担架上躺着脊柱裂患者，就该顺手核查手套和器材含不含乳胶——乳胶过敏是这个病的标配之一。

atScene.en: Down syndrome airway kit adjustments, from the chapter's own case: expect smaller faces — prepare smaller-than-usual equipment, pad under the flat occiput, and budget extra patience for airway management.
atScene.zh: 唐氏患者的气道装备调整，出自本章案例复盘：脸部偏小——备比常规小一号的器材，扁平的后枕下要垫垫料，气道管理多留一份耐心。

atScene.en: Many people with Down syndrome function actively in society and can take part in their own care — talk to the patient, not only the caregiver, and let them assist you in the emergency.
atScene.zh: 许多唐氏患者是社会中能正常生活的一员，完全可以参与自己的医疗——要跟患者本人对话，而不是只对照护者说话，并让他在急救中搭把手。

confusions.en: Conductive versus sensorineural deafness: conductive is usually curable and temporary (eardrum injury, infection, earwax); sensorineural is permanent (inner ear or eighth cranial nerve damage). An option calling earwax-related loss 'permanent' or nerve damage 'curable' has swapped the pair.
confusions.zh: 传导性与感音神经性耳聋：传导性通常可治、属暂时（鼓膜损伤、感染、耵聍）；感音神经性是永久的（内耳或第八对脑神经损伤）。选项把耵聍性听损说成『永久』、把神经损伤说成『可治』，就是把这对概念调了包。

confusions.en: Speaking louder to the hearing-impaired: 80% of hearing loss involves high-pitched sounds, so volume is the wrong axis — LOWER the pitch, or hand the interview to a low-voiced teammate. Some patients are actually oversensitive to loud sound near the ear.
confusions.zh: 对听障患者提高音量：80%的听力损失砸在高频音上，所以音量根本不是正确的调节轴——要『压低音调』，或干脆换个嗓音低沉的队友来问。何况有的患者对贴耳的大声反而过度敏感。

confusions.en: Dysarthria versus aphasia: dysarthria is a muscle-control problem — the sounds come out wrong; aphasia is a language-centre problem — speech, writing, and signs can all fail. One is articulation hardware, the other is language software.
confusions.zh: 构音困难与失语症：构音困难是肌肉控制问题——音发不对；失语症是语言中枢问题——说、写、打手势可能全线失灵。一个坏在『发音硬件』，一个坏在『语言软件』。

confusions.en: Open-ended questions are NOT the default for aphasia: chapter 10's preference reverses here — use focused questions, minimize background noise, and still talk to the patient as an adult.
confusions.zh: 对失语患者不能默认用开放式提问：第10章的偏好在这里要反着用——改用聚焦式问题、压低背景噪音，同时仍然把患者当成年人对话。

confusions.en: 'Cerebral palsy means intellectual disability': 75% have some — meaning a quarter have none, and the disorder itself is nonprogressive. Assuming incompetence in a CP patient is both clinically wrong and a rapport killer.
confusions.zh: 『脑瘫等于智力障碍』：75%的患者有某种程度的智障——反过来说四分之一完全没有，而且脑瘫本身是非进行性的。预设脑瘫患者『不懂事』，既是临床错误，也当场毁掉融洽关系。

confusions.en: Paralysis does not equal absent sensation: some paralyzed patients feel normally, and some have hyperesthesia where touch registers as pain. Conversely, the ones who feel nothing cannot warn you that you are hurting them — two opposite traps from one assumption.
confusions.zh: 瘫痪不等于没感觉：有的瘫痪患者感觉完好，有的还感觉过敏——一碰就是疼。反过来，真没感觉的患者也无法提醒你『你正弄疼我』——一个想当然，两头都是坑。

confusions.en: Autism pain response read backwards: minimal reaction can hide a significant injury, while minor contact can cause great discomfort. Neither the calm nor the distress maps linearly to severity — examine systematically, distal to proximal, explaining first.
confusions.zh: 自闭症的疼痛反应容易读反：重伤可以几乎没反应，轻碰却可能痛苦不堪。淡定和崩溃都不与伤情线性对应——必须系统查体，由远及近，动手前先解释。

confusions.en: Family wants CPR but a DNR exists: the reflex answer 'the DNR always wins' is wrong in this textbook. Make the family aware of the order; if they still insist, start resuscitation — field crews cannot verify the order's provenance, and the sorting-out belongs to the emergency department.
confusions.zh: 家属要求CPR但现场有DNR：条件反射的『DNR永远优先』在这本教材里是错的。先让家属知道指令的存在；知情后仍坚持，就开始复苏——现场无法核实指令的来龙去脉，这团乱麻归急诊科去理。

mnemonics.name: 聋两型：传『暂』感『久』
mnemonics.en: Conductive = Correctable (temporary: drum, infection, wax); Sensorineural = Stays (permanent: inner ear, cranial nerve VIII).
mnemonics.zh: 传导性＝『暂』（可治的暂时问题：鼓膜、感染、耵聍）；感音神经性＝『久』（永久：内耳、第八对脑神经）。传暂感久，四字定型。

mnemonics.name: 言语四障：音·语·流·声
mnemonics.en: The four speech-disorder families — Articulation (dysarthria), Language (aphasia), Fluency (stuttering), Voice production (hoarseness to aphonia).
mnemonics.zh: 言语障碍四大家族——『音』构音障碍（dysarthria）、『语』语言障碍（失语症）、『流』流畅性障碍（口吃）、『声』发声障碍（声嘶到失音）。音语流声，一字一族。

mnemonics.name: 瘫三级：偏·截·四
mnemonics.en: Hemiplegia = one side (stroke/head injury); paraplegia = lower body (thoracic/lumbar cord, spina bifida); quadriplegia = four limbs plus trunk (cervical cord).
mnemonics.zh: 偏瘫＝一侧（卒中/头伤）；截瘫＝下半身（胸腰段脊髓、脊柱裂）；四肢瘫＝四肢加躯干（颈髓）。偏截四，从半边到全身。

mnemonics.name: 自闭接触令：静·释·远近
mnemonics.en: Quiet the scene (excess stimuli trigger), explain before every touch, then contact distal to proximal — and repeat questions in different phrasings to test consistency.
mnemonics.zh: 先『静』场（刺激过载会引爆）、每碰必先『释』（解释）、触碰顺序『由远及近』——再把同一问题换几种问法，验证回答一致性。

selfCheck.qEn: Classify: earwax buildup versus damage to the eighth cranial nerve — which type of deafness, and which is permanent?
selfCheck.qZh: 分类题：耵聍堆积与第八对脑神经损伤——各属哪种耳聋？哪种是永久的？
selfCheck.aEn: Earwax causes conductive deafness — usually curable and temporary. Eighth-nerve (or inner-ear) damage causes sensorineural deafness — permanent.
selfCheck.aZh: 耵聍造成传导性耳聋——通常可治、属暂时。第八对脑神经（或内耳）损伤造成感音神经性耳聋——永久性。

selfCheck.qEn: A hearing aid whistles after insertion, and a second attempt fails. What next? And name the switch positions you check on a dead aid.
selfCheck.qZh: 助听器戴上就啸叫，第二次尝试也失败。接下来怎么办？排查没声的助听器时要看哪个开关挡位？
selfCheck.aEn: Whistling means poor seal or excess volume — reposition or turn it down; after two failed attempts, box the aid, take it along, and document the transfer. On a dead aid check power, fresh battery, tubing, the M (microphone) versus T (telephone) switch, a spare cord for body aids, and wax in the ear mould.
selfCheck.aZh: 啸叫说明未密封或音量过大——调整位置或调低音量；尝试两次不成就装盒带走并记录移交。没声时查：开机、换新电池、导管、开关在M（麦克风）而非T（电话）挡、体挂式换备用导线、耳模是否被耵聍堵住。

selfCheck.qEn: Give the Down syndrome numbers: chromosome count in the affected ovum, the cardiac complication rate, and the airway plan for obstruction.
selfCheck.qZh: 报出唐氏综合征的数字：受累卵子的染色体数、心脏并发症比例、以及气道梗阻时的处置。
selfCheck.aEn: Chromosome 21 fails to separate so the ovum carries 24 chromosomes (trisomy 21 after fertilization); up to 40% have congenital heart disease; for airway obstruction a simple jaw-thrust may suffice — jaw-thrust or nasopharyngeal airway in the unconscious patient, with smaller equipment and padding under the flat occiput.
selfCheck.aZh: 第21号染色体未分离，卵子带24条染色体（受精后成21三体）；先天性心脏病比例可达40%；气道梗阻时简单托颌法可能就够——昏迷者用托颌法或鼻咽通气道，器材小一号、扁平后枕下垫垫料。

selfCheck.qEn: Multiple sclerosis: who does it strike most, which form dominates, and what happens to untreated relapsing/remitting patients?
selfCheck.qZh: 多发性硬化：最好发于谁？哪个型占大头？复发缓解型不治疗会怎样？
selfCheck.aEn: Women in their 20s to 40s, two to three times more often than men; relapsing/remitting accounts for 90% (progressive 10%); untreated, half of relapsing/remitting patients develop the progressive form within 15 years.
selfCheck.aZh: 20～40多岁女性，发病率是男性的2～3倍；复发缓解型占90%（进展型10%）；不治疗的话，复发缓解型患者一半会在15年内转为进展型。

selfCheck.qEn: Which two allergies/equipment facts travel with severe spina bifida?
selfCheck.qZh: 重型脊柱裂随身携带哪两个『过敏/装备』考点？
selfCheck.aEn: Latex allergy is part of the standard package — check your gloves and kit; and 70% to 90% have hydrocephalus managed by a lifelong cerebrospinal-fluid shunt.
selfCheck.aZh: 乳胶过敏是标配——先核查手套和器材；另有70%～90%合并脑积水，靠终身佩戴的脑脊液分流管减压。

selfCheck.qEn: Myasthenia gravis: mechanism in one sentence, the typical first symptom, and the crisis you must anticipate.
selfCheck.qZh: 重症肌无力：一句话机制、典型首发症状、必须预判的危象。
selfCheck.aEn: Antibodies block or damage acetylcholine receptor sites at the nerve junction, so impulses fail to reach muscle; first symptoms are usually weakness of eye or eyelid movement; the crisis is acute respiratory failure when infection, stress, medication effects, or menstruation weaken the respiratory muscles — manage airway, support ventilation, possibly intubate.
selfCheck.aZh: 抗体阻断或破坏神经接头的乙酰胆碱受体位点，冲动传不到肌肉；首发症状通常是眼球或眼睑运动无力；危象是感染、应激、药物作用甚至月经拖垮呼吸肌后的急性呼吸衰竭——气道管理、通气支持、必要时插管。

selfCheck.qEn: The family demands CPR; the patient has a DNR. Sequence your actions per the textbook.
selfCheck.qZh: 家属坚决要求CPR，患者却有DNR。按教材排出你的动作顺序。
selfCheck.aEn: Ensure the family knows the DNR exists; if they still insist once aware, start resuscitation — the field cannot verify who initiated the order or whether legal medical authority is present, and the emergency physicians sort it out. Any doubt about validity alone also means resuscitate while contacting direct medical control.
selfCheck.aZh: 先确保家属知道DNR的存在；知情后仍坚持，就开始复苏——现场无法核实指令由谁启动、有无法定医疗决定权人在场，交给急诊医生去理清。单纯对指令效力存疑时，同样是边复苏边联系直接医疗指挥。

bcAlerts.topicEn: DNR at cardiac arrest: BC's wording is 'verifiable DNR or No CPR order'
bcAlerts.topicZh: 心搏骤停时的DNR：BC 的措辞是『可核实的 DNR 或 No CPR 指令』
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook says CPR is not indicated with a valid DNR, and any doubt about validity means resuscitating while contacting direct medical control; families aware of the order who still insist get resuscitation.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材说有有效DNR就不做CPR，对效力存任何疑问就边复苏边联系医疗指挥；家属知情后仍坚持的，照做复苏。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's exam guidelines put it in the CPR/AED protocol itself: the only contraindication to CPR and AED in cardiac arrest is a VERIFIABLE Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) or No CPR order — note the BC-specific 'No CPR' terminology — and resuscitation continues until the patient recovers, advanced care providers (e.g., BCAS, physician) take over, or such a valid order is presented. If you cannot verify it on scene, you work the arrest.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 考试指南把这条直接写进 CPR/AED 流程：心搏骤停时做 CPR 和 AED 的唯一禁忌，是『可核实的』DNR 或 No CPR 指令——注意 BC 特有的『No CPR』叫法——复苏要持续到患者恢复、高级救护人员（如 BCAS、医生）接手、或有人出示这样一份有效指令为止。现场核实不了，就继续抢救。
bcAlerts.ref: EMALB BC Provincial Examination Guidelines p.40–41（Current to June 15, 2026）
